simple.meaning: נָגַהּ (nâgahh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to glitter ; causatively, to illuminate.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 6 times in 2 Samuel, Job, Psalms, Isaiah, beginning at 2 Samuel 22:29. The surrounding contexts include land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָגַהּ (H5050) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: נָגַהּ (nâgahh) / H5050 is traced through 2 Samuel 22:29, Job 18:5, Job 22:28, Psalms 18:29 with source-language evidence and verse context.

timeline.evidenceText: For you are my lamp, Yahweh.
“Yes, the light of the wicked will be put out.
You will also decree a thing, and it will be established to you.
For by you, I advance through a troop.

But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time he has made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
For the stars of the sky and its constellations will not give their light. The sun will be darkened in its going out, and the moon will not cause its light to shine.
